chunks: I praise Him seeking completion of His Blessing, submitting to His Glory, and seeking safety from His disobedience,
I invoke His help [as one] in need of His Sufficiency,
Indeed, He whom He guides does not go astray, and He with whom He is hostile gets no protection, and He whom He supports does not remain needy;
For He is the heaviest of all that is weighed, and the most valuable of all that is treasured.

key_terms.اسْتِمَامًا: seeking completion or bringing to an end
key_terms.كِفَايَتِهِ: His Sufficiency or protection from need
key_terms.يَئِلُ: to be protected or to have a refuge

ai.seo_question: What are the key aspects of praising Allah and seeking His sufficiency in this supplication from Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this supplication from *Du'a al-Faraj* (often cited in the context of the Age of Ignorance and the Household of Muhammad), Imam Ali (AS) articulates a theological framework of *istitmam* (seeking completion of grace) and *isti'mam* (seeking protection from sin), reflecting the Shia emphasis on divine sufficiency (*kifayah*) as the ultimate remedy for human neediness. The concluding metaphor of weighing and storing highlights Allah's attributes as the most substantial and precious reality, a concept deeply resonant with Shia exegetical traditions that view divine presence as the anchor of spiritual stability. This passage underscores the reciprocal relationship between human reliance on God and God's absolute self-sufficiency, a core tenet in *Tawhid* theology.
